text: Before, you'd waste time watching your AI think out loud; now Inkling Two Mini thinks more in its head, so you wait less, but how?
Here's how, in one hard exam question.
An ordinary model, like Gemma or Kwen, thinks by writing: line after line, and you wait for every line.
Same question on Thinking Machines' Inkling Two Mini, out November twentieth: it does more of the working in its head, then writes a short note.
Its middle twelve layers run three times, same weights: forty-eight layer steps from twenty-four layers, no bigger brain.
In the maker's test on a research twin, three passes wrote less than half the reasoning.
And it's open: about twenty gigabytes, for a thirty-two gig Mac.
That's how you wait less: less thinking to write out.
The catch: each word it writes takes more work, so speed depends on your setup, and it still writes some.
Same exam; more of the working happens in its head.
